paragraphs.text: Most people assume that multitasking allows them to get more done. Research suggests the opposite. When we switch between tasks, the brain needs time to adjust to the new set of rules, and these 'switch costs' can reduce productivity by as much as 40%. Interestingly, people who multitask most often tend to be worse at filtering out irrelevant information than those who rarely do so, although it is not yet clear whether heavy multitasking causes this weakness or whether people who are easily distracted are simply drawn to multitasking.
